html:
The Duchy of Parma and Piacenza was a small state in the Po valley of northern Italy, from 1545 to 1859. It is on the map from 1650 to 1815.

It was carved out of the Papal States in 1545 by Pope Paul III, born Alessandro Farnese, for his own son. The Farnese ruled it until their line died out in 1731. The last Farnese heiress, Elisabeth Farnese, had married the king of Spain, and her sons claimed the duchy; from 1748 a Spanish Bourbon branch held it.

Napoleon's France took it over in 1802. In 1814 it was given to his second wife, Marie Louise, who ruled it until her death in 1847. The Bourbons came back, but in 1859 and 1860 the duchy voted to join Piedmont-Sardinia, on the way to Italy.
sum: The Duchy of Parma and Piacenza was a small state in the Po valley of northern Italy, from 1545 to 1859. It is on the map from 1650 to 1815.
